knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Models and source

Mukherjee 2018 analysed the 8-week phase 2 dose-ranging induction trial of
tofacitinib in moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis (A3921063,
NCT00787202). A one-compartment population PK model supplied each patient's
steady-state average and trough concentrations (C~av,ss~, C~trough,ss~), and
landmark logistic regressions related week-8 efficacy to three exposure
metrics: dose, C~av,ss~ and C~trough,ss~. The paper reports all nine
exposure-response fits (three endpoints by three metrics) in Table 2, so each
is a separate model file; all ten files share this vignette.

| Model | Output | Drug term | Covariates on the logit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib` | `Cc` (ng/mL) | 1-compartment, first-order absorption, lag | none |
| `..._clinrem_dose` / `_cav` / `_ctrough` | `prob_clinrem` | Emax | baseline total Mayo score, baseline CRP |
| `..._clinresp_dose` / `_cav` / `_ctrough` | `prob_clinresp` | linear | baseline total Mayo score, baseline CRP |
| `..._endoimp_dose` / `_cav` | `prob_endoimp` | linear | baseline total Mayo score, prior TNFi failure |
| `..._endoimp_ctrough` | `prob_endoimp` | Emax | baseline total Mayo score, prior TNFi failure |

Endpoint definitions (Methods, "Efficacy assessments"):

* **Clinical remission** (`prob_clinrem`): total Mayo score <= 2 with no
  individual subscore > 1.
* **Clinical response** (`prob_clinresp`, the trial's primary endpoint): a
  decrease from baseline in total Mayo score of >= 3 points and >= 30%, with a
  decrease in rectal-bleeding subscore of >= 1 point or an absolute
  rectal-bleeding subscore of 0 or 1.
* **Mucosal healing** (`prob_endoimp`): Mayo endoscopic subscore of 0 or 1,
  derived post hoc. The library calls this absolute <= 1 endoscopic criterion
  endoscopic improvement.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.13523> (open access, PMC5980553). The
  Supporting Information holds Figures S1-S5 only, with no parameter values.
  No erratum was found (Europe PMC citation search, 2026-11-25).

```{r load-models}
# readModelDb() returns the model function; rxode2::rxode() parses it once.
mod_pk <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib"))

er_names <- c(
  clinrem_dose = "Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib_clinrem_dose",
  clinrem_cav = "Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib_clinrem_cav",
  clinrem_ctrough = "Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib_clinrem_ctrough",
  clinresp_dose = "Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib_clinresp_dose",
  clinresp_cav = "Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib_clinresp_cav",
  clinresp_ctrough = "Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib_clinresp_ctrough",
  endoimp_dose = "Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib_endoimp_dose",
  endoimp_cav = "Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib_endoimp_cav",
  endoimp_ctrough = "Mukherjee_2018_tofacitinib_endoimp_ctrough"
)
mod_er <- lapply(er_names, function(nm) rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(nm)))
```

# Population

Table 1 of Mukherjee 2018 summarises the 188 analysed patients: 47 on placebo
and 31, 32, 30 and 48 on tofacitinib 0.5, 3, 10 and 15 mg twice daily. Of the
194 treated patients, five had no plasma concentrations and one was never
treated; those six were excluded. The patients had a mean age of 42.1 years
(range 19-77), a mean weight of 74.8 kg (41.4-126), and 54.8% were male. Mean
baseline total Mayo score was 8.2 (SD 1.6, range 3-12) and mean baseline CRP
13.9 mg/L (SD 21, range 0.2-124). At baseline 43.1% were on corticosteroids,
and 18.6% had failed a TNF inhibitor in the previous 12 months. The PK model
was fitted to the 141 tofacitinib-treated patients, using samples taken before
dosing and 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2-3 h after it at the baseline and week-8 visits.

# Source trace

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: 1-compartment, first-order absorption, lag | -- | Results, "Pharmacokinetics" |
| CL/F (`lcl`) | 22.4 L/h | Results, "Pharmacokinetics" |
| V/F (`lvc`) | 94.2 L | Results, "Pharmacokinetics" |
| Ka (`lka`) | 2.83 1/h | Results, "Pharmacokinetics" |
| Lag time (`ltlag`) | 0.16 h, fixed | Results, "Pharmacokinetics" |
| IIV CL/F (`etalcl`) | 31.4% CV | Results, "Pharmacokinetics" |
| IIV Ka (`etalka`) | 87.5% CV | Results, "Pharmacokinetics" |
| Residual (`propSd`) | 47.5% | Results, "Pharmacokinetics" |
| C~av,ss~ = Dose / (12 CL/F) | -- | Equation 1 |
| C~trough,ss~ closed form | -- | Equation 2 |
| logit p = beta0 + betaD + sum(beta_m X_m) | -- | Methods, "Data analysis and modelling" |
| betaD = Emax C / (E50 + C) or slope * C | -- | Methods, "Data analysis and modelling" |
| Intercept `logite0`, `emax_*`, `led50_*` / `lec50_*`, `lslope_*` | per model | Table 2 |
| `e_crp_*`, `e_score_mayo_*`, `e_biologic_ir_*` | per model | Table 2 |
| Mayo score divisor 12, CRP divisor 7 mg/L | -- | identified by the maintainers (section "Covariate scaling") |

Table 2 transcribed (point estimate and 95% CI as printed):

| Endpoint | Metric | Intercept | Emax | E50 | Slope | CRP | Mayo | Prior TNFi |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Remission | Dose | 1.81 (-0.35, 3.97) | 2.35 (1.25, 3.45) | 1.06 mg (0.17, 6.49) | | -0.104 | -5.97 | |
| Remission | C~av,ss~ | 1.83 (-0.33, 3.99) | 2.35 (1.25, 3.45) | 3.86 ng/mL (0.63, 23.55) | | -0.105 | -6 | |
| Remission | C~trough,ss~ | 1.91 (-0.23, 4.05) | 2.35 (1.26, 3.44) | 0.84 ng/mL (0.14, 4.86) | | -0.105 | -6.04 | |
| Response | Dose | 0.951 (-0.84, 2.74) | | | 0.11 /mg (0.07, 0.18) | -0.103 | -1.85 | |
| Response | C~av,ss~ | 0.93 (-0.87, 2.73) | | | 0.03 per ng/mL (0.02, 0.05) | -0.104 | -1.81 | |
| Response | C~trough,ss~ | 1.08 (-0.69, 2.85) | | | 0.12 per ng/mL (0.07, 0.22) | -0.0981 | -1.84 | |
| Mucosal healing | Dose | 3.21 (1.37, 5.05) | | | 0.08 /mg (0.04, 0.15) | | -5.18 | -0.798 |
| Mucosal healing | C~av,ss~ | 3.25 (1.41, 5.09) | | | 0.02 per ng/mL (0.01, 0.04) | | -5.15 | -0.805 |
| Mucosal healing | C~trough,ss~ | 3.12 (1.27, 4.97) | 1.41 (0.41, 2.41) | 1.71 ng/mL (0.13, 21.85) | | | -5.35 | -0.789 |

The CIs of E50 and of the slopes are symmetric on the log scale, not the
linear one: for example ln(1.06) - ln(0.17) = 1.83 = ln(6.49) - ln(1.06). Table
2's footnote also flags E50 as "(log scale)". Both are therefore carried as log
parameters (`led50_*`, `lec50_*`, `lslope_*`); the intercepts, Emax and the
covariate coefficients have linearly symmetric CIs and are carried as printed.

# Pharmacokinetics

## Typical-value checks

The paper states a half-life of 2.9 h "based on mean CL/F and V/F estimates".

```{r pk-typical}
th <- mod_pk$theta
cl_typ <- exp(th[["lcl"]])
v_typ <- exp(th[["lvc"]])
ka_typ <- exp(th[["lka"]])
thalf <- log(2) * v_typ / cl_typ
round(thalf, 3)
stopifnot(abs(thalf - 2.9) < 0.05)
```

## Simulated cohort at steady state

Each arm is 200 virtual patients dosed twice daily for 7 days, observed
densely over the last 12-h interval (156-168 h). The paper derives C~av,ss~
from Equation 1 and C~trough,ss~ from Equation 2, using individual parameters.
Both are computed here from each simulated patient's own `ka`, `cl` and `vc`.
PKNCA is then run on the simulated profiles.

```{r pk-cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180601)
arms <- c(0.5, 3, 10, 15)
n_per_arm <- 200
dose_times <- seq(0, 156, by = 12)
obs_times <- 156 + c(0, seq(0.05, 1, by = 0.05), seq(1.25, 12, by = 0.25))

subjects <- tibble(id = seq_len(n_per_arm * length(arms)),
                   dose_mg = rep(arms, each = n_per_arm))
pk_events <- bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(subjects, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(amt = dose_mg, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::expand_grid(subjects, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, evid, cmt, dose_mg)

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, pk_events, keep = "dose_mg",
                       returnType = "data.frame")

# Equation 2 of Mukherjee 2018 (absorption lag ignored, as in the paper).
ctrough_eq2 <- function(dose_mg, ka, cl, v, tau = 12) {
  k <- cl / v
  1000 * dose_mg * ka / (v * (ka - k)) *
    (exp(-k * tau) / (1 - exp(-k * tau)) - exp(-ka * tau) / (1 - exp(-ka * tau)))
}

indiv <- sim |>
  group_by(id) |>
  slice(1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(id, dose_mg, ka, cl, vc,
            cav_eq1 = 1000 * dose_mg / (12 * cl),
            ctrough_eq2 = ctrough_eq2(dose_mg, ka, cl, vc))
```

```{r pk-profile, fig.cap = "Simulated steady-state profiles over the last dosing interval (median and 5th-95th percentiles). Compare with the shape of Figure S1 of Mukherjee 2018, which plots the same quantities on a log scale."}
sim |>
  mutate(tad = time - 156, arm = factor(paste(dose_mg, "mg b.d."),
                                        levels = paste(arms, "mg b.d."))) |>
  group_by(arm, tad) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Tofacitinib (ng/mL)")
```

## PKNCA

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(arm = paste(dose_mg, "mg b.d.")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, arm)
dose_df <- pk_events |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
  mutate(arm = paste(dose_mg, "mg b.d.")) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, arm)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 156, end = 168, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE,
                        auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

# The trough is read directly off the profile 12 h after the last dose; with a
# 0.16 h lag the interval minimum (cmin) falls just after the dose instead.
ctrough_df <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time == max(obs_times)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(arm = paste(dose_mg, "mg b.d."), id, PPTESTCD = "ctrough", PPORRES = Cc)
nca_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
    dplyr::select(arm, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
    mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))),
  ctrough_df |> mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id)))
)
stopifnot(!anyNA(nca_long$PPORRES), sum(nca_long$PPTESTCD == "ctrough") == nrow(indiv))
```

The numerical C~av,ss~ (PKNCA AUC~tau~ / 12) uses the same drawn parameters
as Equation 1, so the two differ only by trapezoidal error. The numerical
trough is taken at 12 h after the dose, which is 11.84 h after the end of the
lag, while Equation 2 ignores the lag. So the simulated trough sits above
Equation 2 by about exp(k * 0.16), roughly 4% for the typical patient.

```{r pk-identity}
chk <- nca_long |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cav", "ctrough")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  mutate(id = as.integer(as.character(id))) |>
  dplyr::left_join(indiv, by = "id") |>
  mutate(cav_err_pct = 100 * (cav / cav_eq1 - 1),
         trough_ratio = ctrough / ctrough_eq2)
summary(chk$cav_err_pct)
summary(chk$trough_ratio)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(chk$cav_err_pct)) < 2,
  median(chk$trough_ratio) > 1, median(chk$trough_ratio) < 1.10
)
```

## Comparison with Figure 1

Figure 1 of Mukherjee 2018 plots the individual C~av,ss~ and C~trough,ss~
values with their medians by dose. The medians were digitised by the
maintainers from the black median symbols after calibrating the axes on their
tick marks.

```{r fig1-compare}
fig1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,          ~cav,  ~ctrough,
  "0.5 mg b.d.", 1.55,  0.21,
  "3 mg b.d.",   10.6,  2.02,
  "10 mg b.d.",  35.9,  7.08,
  "15 mg b.d.",  51.3,  9.55
)
sim_metrics <- indiv |>
  mutate(arm = paste(dose_mg, "mg b.d.")) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, id, cav = cav_eq1, ctrough = ctrough_eq2) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(cav, ctrough), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "PPORRES")

nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_metrics,
  reference = fig1,
  by = "arm",
  units = c(cav = "ng/mL", ctrough = "ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated (Equations 1 and 2) vs. digitised Figure 1 medians. * differs by >20%.")
```

At 3-15 mg the simulated C~av,ss~ medians sit 2-11% above Figure 1 and the
troughs 4-24% above. The paper's medians come from post hoc estimates of
30-48 patients per arm, which are shrunk towards the typical value. At
0.5 mg both symbols sit within a few pixels of zero on the figure's axes: one
pixel is 0.2 ng/mL for C~av,ss~ and 0.1 ng/mL for C~trough,ss~. Those two
medians therefore cannot be read to better than tens of percent, and the
starred rows there are a reading limit.

```{r fig1-gate}
pct_cav <- sim_metrics |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(med = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig1, by = "arm") |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * (med / cav - 1))
# Structural check on the centre: a mistranscribed CL/F, dose or unit moves
# every arm by tens of percent.
stopifnot(abs(median(pct_cav$pct)) < 15)
# The population median of Cav per mg is exactly 1000 / (12 * CL/F) because
# the CL/F random effect is log-normal.
cav_per_mg <- median(indiv$cav_eq1 / indiv$dose_mg)
c(simulated = cav_per_mg, typical = 1000 / (12 * cl_typ))
stopifnot(abs(cav_per_mg / (1000 / (12 * cl_typ)) - 1) < 0.05)
```

# Covariate scaling

Table 2 prints the coefficients for baseline total Mayo score and baseline CRP
but not the scale on which the covariates enter. Read per raw unit they cannot
be right. A coefficient of -5.97 per Mayo point would lower the odds of
remission 390-fold for one point of baseline severity, and the remission
intercept of 1.81 then gives no plausible placebo rate. The maintainers
identified the scaling from three independent pieces of evidence in the paper,
all computed below on a deterministic virtual cohort:

* Baseline Mayo score uses the Table 1 distribution (mean 8.2, SD 1.6,
  integers 3-12).
* CRP is log-normal with the Table 1 mean of 13.9 mg/L and SD of 21 mg/L.
* Prior TNFi failure occurs in 18.6% of patients.
* The arm sizes are those of the trial.

```{r cohort}
mayo_lv <- 3:12
mayo_w <- diff(pnorm(c(-Inf, seq(3.5, 11.5, by = 1), Inf), 8.2, 1.6))
crp_sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (21 / 13.9)^2))
crp_meanlog <- log(13.9) - crp_sdlog^2 / 2
crp_quant <- function(k) qlnorm((seq_len(k) - 0.5) / k, crp_meanlog, crp_sdlog)

make_cohort <- function(k_crp) {
  tidyr::expand_grid(SCORE_MAYO = mayo_lv, CRP = crp_quant(k_crp),
                     BIOLOGIC_IR = 0:1) |>
    mutate(w = mayo_w[match(SCORE_MAYO, mayo_lv)] / k_crp *
             ifelse(BIOLOGIC_IR == 1, 0.186, 0.814))
}
arm_n <- c(`0` = 47, `0.5` = 31, `3` = 32, `10` = 30, `15` = 48)
expit <- function(x) 1 / (1 + exp(-x))
```

**1. Placebo rates.** The intercept multiplies "zero covariate", so the
placebo rate predicted for the trial population depends directly on the
divisor. Dividing the Mayo score by 12 (the maximum of the scale) reproduces
the observed placebo rates of all three endpoints: 0.11, 0.43 and 0.35, from
the bar labels of Figure 2 and Figure S2 and the observed symbol of Figure S5B
digitised by the maintainers. Leaving it unscaled, or dividing by the mean
score, does not.

```{r placebo-rates}
coh <- make_cohort(200)
placebo_rate <- function(endpoint, mayo_div, crp_div) {
  th <- mod_er[[paste0(endpoint, "_dose")]]$theta
  crp_term <- if (endpoint == "endoimp") 0 else th[[paste0("e_crp_", endpoint)]] * coh$CRP / crp_div
  tnf_term <- if (endpoint == "endoimp") th[["e_biologic_ir_endoimp"]] * coh$BIOLOGIC_IR else 0
  eta <- th[["logite0"]] + th[[paste0("e_score_mayo_", endpoint)]] * coh$SCORE_MAYO / mayo_div +
    crp_term + tnf_term
  sum(coh$w * expit(eta))
}
hyp <- tibble::tribble(
  ~hypothesis,                         ~mayo_div, ~crp_div,
  "raw units (as printed)",            1,         1,
  "divided by the population mean",    8.2,       13.9,
  "Mayo / 12, CRP raw (mg/L)",         12,        1,
  "Mayo / 12, CRP in mg/dL (/10)",     12,        10,
  "Mayo / 12, CRP / 7 mg/L (packaged)", 12,       7
)
placebo_tab <- hyp |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(remission = placebo_rate("clinrem", mayo_div, crp_div),
         response = placebo_rate("clinresp", mayo_div, crp_div),
         mucosal_healing = placebo_rate("endoimp", mayo_div, crp_div)) |>
  ungroup()
placebo_tab |>
  dplyr::select(-mayo_div, -crp_div) |>
  dplyr::rename(Hypothesis = hypothesis, Remission = remission,
                Response = response, `Mucosal healing` = mucosal_healing) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Predicted placebo rates; observed 0.11, 0.43 and 0.35.")
pk_row <- placebo_tab[placebo_tab$mayo_div == 12 & placebo_tab$crp_div == 7, ]
stopifnot(
  abs(pk_row$remission - 0.11) < 0.04,
  abs(pk_row$response - 0.43) < 0.08,
  abs(pk_row$mucosal_healing - 0.35) < 0.08,
  placebo_tab$remission[1] < 0.001,
  placebo_tab$response[placebo_tab$mayo_div == 12 & placebo_tab$crp_div == 1] < 0.3
)
```

**2. Confidence-interval widths.** The paper prints a 95% CI for every
estimate. The width of a CI depends on the scale of its covariate through the
Fisher information of the trial's 188 patients. Evaluated at the published
point estimates, the information predicts each CI half-width. The predicted
widths of the remission intercept, Emax and log E50 agree with the printed
ones for a Mayo divisor of 12, and are 40-85% too wide when the score is
divided by its mean. The CRP coefficient's width then places the CRP divisor
near 6.6 mg/L. The response model, checked the same way by the maintainers,
places it near 6 mg/L. Both are close to the population median CRP (7.7 mg/L
for the log-normal matched to Table 1). Raw mg/L makes the CRP interval about
half as wide as printed, and it also fails the placebo-response check
above.

```{r fisher}
fisher_halfwidth <- function(mayo_div, crp_div) {
  th <- mod_er$clinrem_dose$theta
  e50 <- exp(th[["led50_clinrem"]])
  emax <- th[["emax_clinrem"]]
  info <- matrix(0, 5, 5)
  for (d in as.numeric(names(arm_n))) {
    f <- coh$SCORE_MAYO / mayo_div
    g <- coh$CRP / crp_div
    eta <- th[["logite0"]] + emax * d / (e50 + d) + th[["e_crp_clinrem"]] * g +
      th[["e_score_mayo_clinrem"]] * f
    p <- expit(eta)
    # gradient of eta wrt (intercept, Emax, log E50, CRP coef, Mayo coef)
    X <- cbind(1, d / (e50 + d), -emax * d * e50 / (e50 + d)^2, g, f)
    info <- info + arm_n[[as.character(d)]] * crossprod(X, X * (coh$w * p * (1 - p)))
  }
  1.96 * sqrt(diag(solve(info)))
}
printed <- c(intercept = 2.16, emax = 1.10, log_e50 = 1.82, crp = 0.155, mayo = 3.23)
ci_tab <- hyp[-1, ] |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(hw = list(setNames(fisher_halfwidth(mayo_div, crp_div), names(printed)))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  tidyr::unnest_wider(hw)
ci_ratio <- ci_tab |>
  mutate(across(all_of(names(printed)), ~ .x / printed[[cur_column()]]))
ci_ratio |>
  dplyr::select(-mayo_div, -crp_div) |>
  dplyr::rename(Hypothesis = hypothesis, Intercept = intercept, Emax = emax,
                `log E50` = log_e50, CRP = crp, Mayo = mayo) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Predicted / printed 95% CI half-width, clinical-remission dose model (1 = exact agreement).")
pk_ci <- unlist(ci_ratio[ci_ratio$mayo_div == 12 & ci_ratio$crp_div == 7, names(printed)])
stopifnot(all(pk_ci > 0.75), all(pk_ci < 1.30))
```

**3. Subgroup predictions.** The paper reports placebo-adjusted remission at
10 mg twice daily of 39% for patients with baseline Mayo score <= 8 and 21% for
those > 8. The packaged clinical-remission dose model gives:

```{r subgroup}
# Weighted remission rate of a cohort at one dose, through the packaged model.
remission_rate <- function(dat, dose) {
  x <- dat |>
    mutate(id = seq_len(n()), time = 0, evid = 0L, DOSE = dose) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, evid, DOSE, SCORE_MAYO, CRP)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_er$clinrem_dose), x, returnType = "data.frame")
  sum(dat$w * out$prob_clinrem) / sum(dat$w)
}
sub_pred <- function(lo) {
  dat <- if (lo) coh[coh$SCORE_MAYO <= 8, ] else coh[coh$SCORE_MAYO > 8, ]
  remission_rate(dat, 10) - remission_rate(dat, 0)
}
subgroup <- c(mayo_le_8 = sub_pred(TRUE), mayo_gt_8 = sub_pred(FALSE))
round(100 * subgroup, 1)
stopifnot(abs(subgroup[["mayo_le_8"]] - 0.39) < 0.05,
          abs(subgroup[["mayo_gt_8"]] - 0.21) < 0.05)
```

The CRP effect is small. Using 10 instead of 7 as the CRP divisor (i.e.
reading the coefficient per mg/dL, the unit of the sponsor's other tofacitinib
datasets) moves every predicted rate in this vignette by less than 2
percentage points.

# Exposure-response predictions

The virtual trial below reuses the deterministic cohort with 20 CRP
quantiles, and gives each patient the exposure of each arm. For the C~av,ss~
and C~trough,ss~ models, exposure is spread over the CL/F and Ka random
effects with equal-probability quadrature nodes. Arms are weighted by their
trial sizes. Each of the nine models is solved through `rxSolve()`.

```{r er-trial}
coh20 <- make_cohort(20)
om <- mod_pk$omega
nodes <- function(k, var) qnorm((seq_len(k) - 0.5) / k) * sqrt(var)
eta_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(eta_cl = nodes(9, om["etalcl", "etalcl"]),
                               eta_ka = nodes(5, om["etalka", "etalka"])) |>
  mutate(w_eta = 1 / n())

trial <- tidyr::expand_grid(coh20, dose_mg = as.numeric(names(arm_n)), eta_grid) |>
  mutate(
    cl = cl_typ * exp(eta_cl),
    ka = ka_typ * exp(eta_ka),
    DOSE = dose_mg,
    CAV = 1000 * dose_mg / (12 * cl),
    CTROUGH = ifelse(dose_mg == 0, 0, ctrough_eq2(dose_mg, ka, cl, v_typ)),
    wt = w * w_eta * arm_n[as.character(dose_mg)] / sum(arm_n)
  )

predict_model <- function(model, data) {
  x <- data |>
    mutate(id = seq_len(n()), time = 0, evid = 0L) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, evid, dplyr::any_of(c("DOSE", "CAV", "CTROUGH",
                                                  "SCORE_MAYO", "CRP", "BIOLOGIC_IR")))
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(model), x, returnType = "data.frame")
  stopifnot(nrow(out) == nrow(data))
  out[[grep("^prob_", names(out), value = TRUE)]]
}
trial_pred <- trial
for (nm in names(mod_er)) trial_pred[[nm]] <- predict_model(mod_er[[nm]], trial)

arm_rates <- trial_pred |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(all_of(names(mod_er)), names_to = "model", values_to = "p") |>
  group_by(model, dose_mg) |>
  summarise(rate = sum(wt * p) / sum(wt), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::separate(model, c("endpoint", "metric"), sep = "_")
```

## Dose, C~av,ss~ and C~trough,ss~ give the same arm-level predictions

The paper's central finding is that the three exposure metrics are
interchangeable predictors of efficacy. With every patient carrying the
exposure their arm produces, the three fitted models for each endpoint should
therefore give nearly the same arm-level rates.

```{r metric-agreement}
arm_rates |>
  mutate(rate = round(100 * rate, 1)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = rate) |>
  dplyr::rename(Endpoint = endpoint, `Dose (mg b.d.)` = dose_mg,
                `Dose model (%)` = dose, `Cav,ss model (%)` = cav,
                `Ctrough,ss model (%)` = ctrough) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Predicted response rate by arm for each of the nine models.")
spread <- arm_rates |>
  group_by(endpoint, dose_mg) |>
  summarise(range_pp = 100 * diff(range(rate)), .groups = "drop")
# Deterministic quadrature; observed when written: at most 6.8 percentage points.
stopifnot(max(spread$range_pp) < 8, median(spread$range_pp) < 4)
```

```{r fig-er, fig.cap = "Predicted week-8 response rates by arm for the dose, Cav,ss and Ctrough,ss models of each endpoint, with the observed proportions of Figure 2, Figure S2 and Figure S5B (crosses)."}
observed <- tibble::tribble(
  ~endpoint,  ~dose_mg, ~obs,
  "clinrem",  0, 0.11, "clinrem", 0.5, 0.13, "clinrem", 3, 0.34, "clinrem", 10, 0.50, "clinrem", 15, 0.42,
  "clinresp", 0, 0.43, "clinresp", 0.5, 0.32, "clinresp", 3, 0.47, "clinresp", 10, 0.60, "clinresp", 15, 0.77,
  "endoimp",  0, 0.35, "endoimp", 0.5, 0.39, "endoimp", 3, 0.47, "endoimp", 10, 0.60, "endoimp", 15, 0.65
)
ggplot(arm_rates, aes(dose_mg, rate, colour = metric)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  geom_point(data = observed, aes(dose_mg, obs), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 4, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  labs(x = "Tofacitinib dose (mg b.d.)", y = "Predicted proportion", colour = "Model")
```

Observed remission and response proportions are the bar labels of Figure 2
and Figure S2. Figure S3 (mucosal healing by dose) is not part of the
Supporting Information file, so the observed mucosal-healing proportions were
digitised from the observed symbols of Figure S5B. The figure shows the
paper's point: response rises steeply between 0.5 and 10 mg and is near its
plateau by 15 mg.

## Comparison with Figure 5 (placebo-adjusted remission)

Figure 5 plots the placebo-adjusted remission predicted by each final model,
by dose and by quartile bin of C~av,ss~ and C~trough,ss~ among the treated
patients. The maintainers digitised the predicted points. Here the quartile
bins are formed from the weighted virtual trial in the same way.

```{r fig5}
fig5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~metric,   ~bin, ~fig,
  "dose",    1, 0.054, "dose",    2, 0.204, "dose",    3, 0.314, "dose",    4, 0.333,
  "cav",     1, 0.084, "cav",     2, 0.203, "cav",     3, 0.331, "cav",     4, 0.350,
  "ctrough", 1, 0.076, "ctrough", 2, 0.182, "ctrough", 3, 0.363, "ctrough", 4, 0.320
)
wquantile <- function(x, w, probs) {
  o <- order(x)
  cw <- cumsum(w[o]) / sum(w)
  vapply(probs, function(p) x[o][which(cw >= p)[1]], numeric(1))
}
active <- trial_pred |> dplyr::filter(dose_mg > 0)
pbo_rem <- trial_pred |>
  dplyr::filter(dose_mg == 0) |>
  summarise(across(starts_with("clinrem"), ~ sum(wt * .x) / sum(wt)))
bin_by <- function(x, w) {
  cuts <- wquantile(x, w, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
  findInterval(x, cuts, left.open = TRUE) + 1
}
fig5_sim <- bind_rows(
  active |> mutate(bin = match(dose_mg, c(0.5, 3, 10, 15))) |>
    group_by(bin) |>
    summarise(sim = sum(wt * clinrem_dose) / sum(wt) - pbo_rem$clinrem_dose) |>
    mutate(metric = "dose"),
  active |> mutate(bin = bin_by(CAV, wt)) |>
    group_by(bin) |>
    summarise(sim = sum(wt * clinrem_cav) / sum(wt) - pbo_rem$clinrem_cav) |>
    mutate(metric = "cav"),
  active |> mutate(bin = bin_by(CTROUGH, wt)) |>
    group_by(bin) |>
    summarise(sim = sum(wt * clinrem_ctrough) / sum(wt) - pbo_rem$clinrem_ctrough) |>
    mutate(metric = "ctrough")
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(fig5, by = c("metric", "bin")) |>
  mutate(diff_pp = 100 * (sim - fig))
fig5_sim |>
  mutate(sim = round(sim, 3), diff_pp = round(diff_pp, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename(Metric = metric, `Dose or quartile bin` = bin,
                Simulated = sim, `Figure 5` = fig, `Difference (pp)` = diff_pp) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Placebo-adjusted remission: deterministic virtual trial vs. digitised Figure 5.")
stopifnot(abs(median(fig5_sim$diff_pp)) < 4, max(abs(fig5_sim$diff_pp)) < 10)
```

## Comparison with Figure S5 (response and mucosal healing)

Figure S5 plots the predictions of the response and mucosal-healing models
against dose for the index trial. The maintainers traced the dose-model
prediction lines at 3, 10 and 15 mg. The paper's simulation used the actual
patients' covariates arm by arm, while this vignette uses one shared cohort,
so agreement is expected only within a few percentage points.

```{r figS5}
figS5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~endpoint,  ~dose_mg, ~fig,
  "clinresp", 3, 0.44, "clinresp", 10, 0.65, "clinresp", 15, 0.73,
  "endoimp",  3, 0.44, "endoimp",  10, 0.57, "endoimp",  15, 0.67
)
figS5_cmp <- arm_rates |>
  dplyr::filter(metric == "dose") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(figS5, by = c("endpoint", "dose_mg")) |>
  mutate(diff_pp = 100 * (rate - fig))
figS5_cmp |>
  mutate(rate = round(rate, 3), diff_pp = round(diff_pp, 1)) |>
  dplyr::select(Endpoint = endpoint, `Dose (mg b.d.)` = dose_mg,
                Simulated = rate, `Figure S5` = fig, `Difference (pp)` = diff_pp) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(abs(median(figS5_cmp$diff_pp)) < 5, max(abs(figS5_cmp$diff_pp)) < 10)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Covariate scaling (not printed).** The paper prints the Mayo and CRP
  coefficients without the scale on which the covariates enter. The packaged
  models use `SCORE_MAYO / 12` and `CRP / 7` (mg/L), both uncentered, as
  identified in the section "Covariate scaling".
  * The Mayo divisor is well determined. The placebo rates of all three
    endpoints, the remission CI widths and the paper's subgroup prediction all
    point to 12, the maximum of the scale.
  * The CRP divisor is determined only to a range of about 6-7.5 mg/L, from
    the CRP CI widths in the remission and response models. 7 mg/L is the
    maintainers' rounded value, close to the population median. Reading CRP per mg/dL (a divisor of 10)
    changes the predictions here by less than 2 percentage points.
* **IIV scale.** The PK random effects are printed as % CV (31.4% on CL/F,
  87.5% on Ka). They were converted to log-normal variances with
  omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2). If the authors instead reported 100 * sqrt(omega^2),
  the Ka variance would be 0.766 rather than 0.569. Ka barely affects C~av,ss~
  and C~trough,ss~.
* **Residual error.** The paper reports "residual variability 47.5%", and
  Figure S1 shows the concentrations on a natural-log scale. It is encoded as
  a proportional error with SD 0.475.
* **Absorption lag.** Fixed at 0.16 h, as the paper did for convergence.
  Equation 2 of the paper ignores the lag when computing C~trough,ss~; the
  `CTROUGH` covariate should be supplied the same way (see the
  `ctrough_eq2()` helper above).
* **Exposure inputs.** The exposure-response models take `DOSE` (mg per
  twice-daily administration), `CAV` or `CTROUGH` (ng/mL) as data columns, set
  to 0 for placebo. They do not call the PK model. When solving with a `DOSE`
  column, include an `evid` column so that rxode2 does not read `DOSE` as the
  dose amount.
* **Prior TNFi failure.** Encoded with the library's `BIOLOGIC_IR` column; the
  source restricts it to anti-TNF failure within the previous 12 months.
* **Placeholder residual.** The exposure-response models carry a fixed
  additive residual SD of 0.001 on the probability output, only so that
  nlmixr2 accepts them for simulation; the source likelihood is Bernoulli.
* **Virtual cohort.** CRP is log-normal (mean 13.9, SD 21 mg/L), the Mayo
  score is a discretised normal (mean 8.2, SD 1.6, 3-12), and prior TNFi
  failure is independent at 18.6%. These are reconstructions from Table 1
  marginals, with covariate correlations ignored.
* **Not packaged.** The base models without covariates shown in Figure 4 have
  no printed estimates. Corticosteroid use, faecal calprotectin, albumin and
  the demographics were screened but not retained in the final models.
